title: Downcasting
summary: Casting a parent reference back to its specialized child and avoiding ClassCastException.

activities.title: Practical Context: Reclaiming Subclass Capabilities Safely

realWorldMetaphor.scenario: Imagine a mechanic reaches into a communal drawer labeled 'Hand Tools'. They pull out an item. Looking at it, it fits the description of a general hand tool. But before attempting to tighten a Torx security bolt, the mechanic must look closely at the tip to confirm: 'Is this specifically a Torx screwdriver?' If it is, they use it for Torx screws. If it's a flathead and they try to force it into a Torx bolt anyway, they strip the bolt immediately!
realWorldMetaphor.mapping: In Java, when you hold a general superclass reference (`Tool t`), the compiler only lets you perform general tool actions. If you want to use specialized subclass capabilities (`torx.tightenSecurityBolt()`), you must perform an explicit downcast `(TorxDriver) t`. If the object on the heap is NOT actually a `TorxDriver`, the JVM throws an immediate `ClassCastException`!
realWorldMetaphor.takeaway: Downcasting requires an explicit cast syntax and must always be verified with instanceof to prevent runtime crashes.

activities.content:
When objects are passed through generalized pipelines as parent types, there are specific situations where code must recover specialized subclass capabilities.

For example, a graphical event dispatcher receives a generic `InputEvent`. When routing to a mouse handler, it downcasts the event to `MouseEvent` to extract coordinate data (`getX()`, `getY()`).

Downcasting enables narrowing conversions, but requires disciplined type checks to prevent fatal runtime exceptions.

activities.title: Downcasting in Java: Definition, Syntax, and ClassCastException Prevention
Unsafe Downcasting vs Guarded Downcasting
activities.explanation: Guarding with instanceof prevents the catastrophic ClassCastException that occurs if an incompatible object (Laptop) is cast to SmartPhone.

stepByStepWalkthrough.description: `d1` holds a `SmartPhone`; `instanceof SmartPhone` evaluates to true.
The cast `(SmartPhone) d1` succeeds and binds `phone`.
`d2` holds a `Laptop`; casting directly to `SmartPhone` would crash at runtime.
Checking `d2 instanceof Laptop` ensures safe downcasting to `Laptop`.

activities.title: Restoring Capabilities in a Plugin Architecture
activities.explanation: Downcasting across interfaces (query interface pattern): tests whether a general Plugin also supports ConfigurablePlugin.

stepByStepWalkthrough.description: `LoggingPlugin` implements `ConfigurablePlugin`, so it downcasts safely and calls `configure()`.

questions.question: What is downcasting in Java?
options: Casting a primitive to a smaller byte size
Casting a superclass reference to a subclass type
Deleting an object from the heap
Overriding a method with private visibility
questions.explanation: Downcasting moves down the inheritance tree, casting a general superclass reference to a more specific subclass.

questions.question: Why does downcasting require explicit syntax `(Subclass) ref` while upcasting does not?
options: Because the compiler cannot verify whether the runtime heap object is truly an instance of the subclass
Because downcasting allocates additional heap memory
Because downcasting disables garbage collection
Because subclasses have smaller bytecode
questions.explanation: Downcasting is potentially unsafe; the developer must explicitly acknowledge the conversion with a cast.

questions.question: What happens if you execute `Animal a = new Animal(); Dog d = (Dog) a;`?
options: a is successfully converted to Dog with default Dog fields
The JVM throws a ClassCastException at runtime
The code fails to compile with an inconvertible types error
d becomes null
questions.explanation: A pure `Animal` instance is not a `Dog`. Casting it throws a runtime `ClassCastException`.

questions.question: What is the best practice before performing a downcast?
options: Always wrap the cast in a try-catch block for NullPointerException
Always test the reference with `instanceof` first
Call System.gc() before casting
Set the reference variable to null
questions.explanation: Guarding downcasts with `if (ref instanceof Subclass)` guarantees type safety and prevents exceptions.

questions.question: Can downcasting modify the fields of the object on the heap?
options: Yes, it resets all fields to default values
No, casting only changes the reference type view, not the heap object itself
Yes, it removes superclass fields
Only if the fields are protected
questions.explanation: Type casting in Java never alters or reallocates the underlying heap object.

questions.question: Which of the following will result in a compile-time error?
options: Object o = "text"; String s = (String) o;
String s = "text"; Integer i = (Integer) s;
Number n = Integer.valueOf(5); Integer i = (Integer) n;
CharSequence cs = "hello"; String s = (String) cs;
questions.explanation: `String` and `Integer` are unrelated classes with no inheritance relationship, so the compiler rejects the cast immediately.

questions.question: What exception is thrown when an illegal downcast executes at runtime?
options: IllegalStateException
ClassCastException
IllegalArgumentException
NullPointerException
questions.explanation: The JVM throws `java.lang.ClassCastException` upon an incompatible downcast.

questions.question: Given `Object obj = null; String s = (String) obj;`, what happens?
options: ClassCastException is thrown
s is assigned null without error
Compile-time error
NullPointerException is thrown
questions.explanation: In Java, casting `null` to any reference type succeeds and simply yields `null`.

questions.question: What is the primary reason developers downcast?
options: To invoke subclass-specific methods that are not declared in the superclass
To improve performance of arithmetic loops
To prevent the object from being garbage collected
To bypass access modifiers
questions.explanation: Downcasting unlocks access to methods and fields declared exclusively on the subclass.

questions.question: If you find yourself writing downcasts everywhere in your codebase, what is likely wrong?
options: You should be using C++ instead
Your OOP abstraction is leaky or insufficient; polymorphic methods should be added to the superclass
Your classes are too small
The JVM version is outdated
questions.explanation: Widespread downcasting is a code smell indicating that the base abstraction fails to provide the necessary common operations.

interviewQA.question: Why is downcasting considered potentially dangerous in Java?
interviewQA.answer: Downcasting is dangerous because the compiler cannot statically guarantee that the reference points to an object of the target subtype at runtime. If the heap object is incompatible, the JVM throws an unchecked `ClassCastException`, which can crash the application in production if unguarded.
interviewQA.expectedAnswer: Downcasting bypasses static compile-time safety and risks runtime ClassCastException if the heap object is incompatible.
interviewQA.keyTakeaway: Downcasting shifts type verification from compile time to runtime.
keyPoints: Downcasting shifts type verification from compile time to runtime.

interviewQA.question: Can you cast an instance of a parent class into a child class? Why or why not?
interviewQA.answer: No. An instance created with `new Parent()` only possesses the state and implementation of the parent. It lacks the specialized fields and behaviors of the child. Attempting `Child c = (Child) new Parent()` throws `ClassCastException` at runtime. Downcasting only works when the object was instantiated as the child in the first place.
interviewQA.expectedAnswer: No. A genuine parent instance does not satisfy the child contract and throws ClassCastException.
interviewQA.keyTakeaway: Downcasting cannot create child state out of thin air; the object must already be a child instance.
keyPoints: Downcasting cannot create child state out of thin air; the object must already be a child instance.

interviewQA.question: What is the bytecode instruction executed when a downcast occurs?
interviewQA.answer: The Java bytecode instruction is `checkcast`. The JVM's execution engine checks the object header against the class token. If the check fails, the JVM raises a `ClassCastException`. If the reference is null or the check succeeds, execution continues.
interviewQA.expectedAnswer: The bytecode instruction is checkcast, which validates the heap object type before completing the cast.
interviewQA.keyTakeaway: Downcasting maps directly to the checkcast bytecode instruction.
keyPoints: Downcasting maps directly to the checkcast bytecode instruction.

interviewQA.question: What is the 'Query Interface' idiom, and how does downcasting enable it?
interviewQA.answer: In extensible architectures (like Eclipse or Spring plugins), components implement multiple capability interfaces. Client code receives a base interface (`Component`) and dynamically 'queries' for additional capabilities using downcasting: `if (c instanceof Auditable) ((Auditable) c).audit()`. This allows optional behaviors without polluting the base interface.
interviewQA.expectedAnswer: Query Interface uses instanceof downcasting to test and activate optional interface capabilities dynamically.
interviewQA.keyTakeaway: Query interface pattern uses downcasting to discover optional capabilities.
keyPoints: Query interface pattern uses downcasting to discover optional capabilities.

interviewQA.question: How can you refactor code to eliminate unnecessary downcasting?
interviewQA.answer: You can eliminate downcasting by: 1) Declaring polymorphic abstract/default methods in the common supertype, 2) Applying the Visitor Pattern to handle subtype-specific operations cleanly, or 3) Leveraging Java generics with bounded type parameters (`<T extends Subtype>`).
interviewQA.expectedAnswer: Eliminate downcasting by pushing common methods to the supertype, using the Visitor pattern, or employing generics.
interviewQA.keyTakeaway: Polymorphism, Visitor Pattern, and Generics eliminate ugly downcasting.
keyPoints: Polymorphism, Visitor Pattern, and Generics eliminate ugly downcasting.

interviewQA.question: What is heap pollution in Java, and how does it relate to casting?
interviewQA.answer: Heap pollution occurs when a variable of a parameterized type refers to an object that is not of that parameterized type, typically caused by mixing raw types and unchecked casts. While the cast appears to succeed initially, an unexpected `ClassCastException` will be thrown later when an element is extracted and cast implicitly by the compiler.
interviewQA.expectedAnswer: Heap pollution happens when generic type erasure masks an incompatible type, causing ClassCastException at extraction.
interviewQA.keyTakeaway: Heap pollution delays ClassCastExceptions to later access points.
keyPoints: Heap pollution delays ClassCastExceptions to later access points.

practiceProblems.title: Warmup: Guarded Account Downcast
practiceProblems.problemStatement:
Complete the account processor:
1. Base class `Account` with `protected String id` and `protected double balance`.
2. Subclass `SavingsAccount extends Account` with method `public void applyInterest(double rate)` adding `balance * rate` to `balance`.
3. In `processInterest(Account acc)`: check if `acc` is an instance of `SavingsAccount`. If so, safely downcast and call `applyInterest(0.05)`.
In `main`, pass a `SavingsAccount("SA-101", 1000.0)` and print the balance: `'Updated Balance: $1050.0'`.

practiceProblems.title: Document Formatter Downcaster
practiceProblems.problemStatement:
Build a document formatting tool from scratch without starter code:
1. Base class `Document` with `protected String title`. Constructor `Document(String title)`. Method `public String getTitle()`.
2. Subclass `PdfDocument extends Document`: constructor `(title, numPages)`. Method `public void renderVectorGraphics()` printing `'Rendering PDF vector graphics across ' + numPages + ' pages'`.
3. Subclass `TextDocument extends Document`: constructor `(title, encoding)`. Method `public void applyWordWrap()` printing `'Applying word wrap with encoding ' + encoding`.
4. Class `DocumentRenderer` with static method `public static void renderSpecialized(Document doc)`:
   - Prints `'Processing document: ' + doc.getTitle()`
   - If `doc instanceof PdfDocument`, safely downcasts and calls `renderVectorGraphics()`
   - If `doc instanceof TextDocument`, safely downcasts and calls `applyWordWrap()`
5. In `Main`, call `renderSpecialized` with a `new PdfDocument("Whitepaper", 14)` and a `new TextDocument("Notes", "UTF-8")`.
practiceProblems.expectedOutput:
Processing document: Whitepaper
Rendering PDF vector graphics across 14 pages
Processing document: Notes
Applying word wrap with encoding UTF-8
hints: DocumentRenderer checks instanceof for PdfDocument and TextDocument.
Downcast explicitly to access renderVectorGraphics() and applyWordWrap().

practiceProblems.title: Smart Audio Mixer Controller
practiceProblems.problemStatement:
Build an audio channel mixer from scratch without starter code:
1. Base class `AudioChannel` with field `channelName` (String). Constructor sets `channelName`. Method `public String getChannelName()`.
2. Subclass `VocalChannel extends AudioChannel`: method `public void autoTune(int pitchCorrection)` printing `'Autotuning ' + channelName + ' by ' + pitchCorrection + ' cents'`.
3. Subclass `BassChannel extends AudioChannel`: method `public void boostSubBass(double db)` printing `'Boosting sub-bass on ' + channelName + ' by ' + db + ' dB'`.
4. Class `MixerDesk` with method `public void processChannels(AudioChannel[] channels)`:
   - Iterates through `channels`
   - If channel is a `VocalChannel`, downcasts and calls `autoTune(25)`
   - If channel is a `BassChannel`, downcasts and calls `boostSubBass(6.0)`
5. In `Main`, create an array `AudioChannel[] desk` holding a `new VocalChannel("Lead Vocal")` and a `new BassChannel("808 Sub")`. Pass it to `MixerDesk.processChannels()`.
practiceProblems.expectedOutput:
Autotuning Lead Vocal by 25 cents
Boosting sub-bass on 808 Sub by 6.0 dB
hints: Use super(name) in VocalChannel and BassChannel constructors.
Process channels with an enhanced for-loop and instanceof downcasts.

practiceProblems.title: Bug Hunt: Blind Downcast in Shape Processing
practiceProblems.problemStatement: The code below blindly downcasts elements of a `Shape` array to `Circle`, crashing with a `ClassCastException` on `Rectangle`. Fix the code by properly checking the type before downcasting, so circles print their radius and rectangles print their dimensions without throwing any exceptions.
hints: Use `if (s instanceof Circle)` for circles and `else if (s instanceof Rectangle)` for rectangles.
Call printRadius() on circle and printDimensions() on rectangle.

practiceProblems.title: Advanced: Safe Heterogeneous Cast Pipeline
practiceProblems.problemStatement:
Build a safe heterogeneous casting pipeline from scratch without starter code:
1. Interface `Command` with `void execute()`.
2. Subclass `RestartCommand implements Command`: `execute()` prints `'Executing system reboot'`.
3. Subclass `BackupCommand implements Command`: fields `destination` (String). Constructor sets `destination`. `execute()` prints `'Executing backup to ' + destination`. Method `public void verifyChecksum()` printing `'Checksum verified for ' + destination`.
4. Class `CommandRunner` with static method `public static void runAndVerify(Command[] batch)`:
   - For each command in `batch`, call `cmd.execute()`
   - If `cmd` is an instance of `BackupCommand`, downcast and call `verifyChecksum()`
5. In `Main`, create an array `Command[] batch` containing `new RestartCommand()` and `new BackupCommand("/mnt/nas/daily.bak")`.
6. Run `runAndVerify(batch)`.
practiceProblems.expectedOutput:
Executing system reboot
Executing backup to /mnt/nas/daily.bak
Checksum verified for /mnt/nas/daily.bak
